issues.legal_issue: A civil court cannot revisit a claimant’s qualification or grant relief inconsistent with a final tribunal determination made in consolidated proceedings concerning rival claims to property.
material_facts: A special tribunal consolidated rival claims concerning property notified as claimed by a religious institution.
The claimant asserted that he was a descendant of the person whose descendants were entitled to manage the property; that assertion was not challenged in the tribunal proceedings.
The tribunal determined that the property was dedicated property managed by that person’s descendants, and the claimant’s opponents did not challenge that determination on appeal.
The claimant later brought a civil suit for possession, and the opponents disputed his descent and entitlement to sue.
issues.conclusion: The opponents could not dispute the claimant’s descent in the civil suit because doing so would question the final tribunal determination and permit relief inconsistent with it.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 15 and 34 of the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925, the tribunal could consolidate rival claims to property and determine the claimants’ rights, with an appeal available to an aggrieved party. Sections 36 and 37 bar a court from questioning anything done by the tribunal under the Act or granting a decree inconsistent with its decision. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: civil_possession_suit and consolidated_tribunal_property_claims and claimant_qualification_was_unchallenged and final_tribunal_decision_identified_eligible_managers and opponent_did_not_challenge_that_decision

predicates.civil_possession_suit: A party brought a civil suit seeking possession of property.
predicates.consolidated_tribunal_property_claims: A tribunal combined rival claims concerning the same property in one proceeding.
predicates.claimant_qualification_was_unchallenged: The claimant relied on a qualification relevant to the property claim, and no participant disputed that qualification before the tribunal.
predicates.final_tribunal_decision_identified_eligi: The tribunal made a final determination identifying the class of persons entitled to manage the property.
predicates.opponent_did_not_challenge_that_decision: An opponent who could challenge the tribunal determination did not do so.
predicates.civil_court_cannot_reopen_claimant_quali: The civil court cannot revisit the claimant’s qualification where doing so would question or contradict the final tribunal determination.

issues.definition: When a civil possession suit follows consolidated tribunal proceedings in which the claimant’s qualification was not disputed and a final decision identified the eligible managers, an opponent who did not challenge that decision cannot reopen the qualification in court.

issues.legal_issue: Possession held as a servant or servitor is permissive, and a possession claim is not time-barred by adverse possession unless hostile possession is established for the applicable limitation period.
material_facts: The defendants possessed the property as servants or servitors, and their possession was permissive.
In the earlier tribunal proceedings, the defendants claimed the status of servitors rather than setting up a hostile title against the claimant.
The suit for possession was filed after those proceedings, but the record did not establish hostile possession for the applicable limitation period.
issues.conclusion: The suit was not barred by limitation under either Article 142 or Article 144 of the Limitation Act, 1908.
issues.legal_principle: Under Articles 142 and 144 of the Limitation Act, 1908, permissive possession does not itself establish adverse possession. Where possession began permissively, the claimant relying on limitation must establish possession hostile to the person entitled to the property for the applicable limitation period; Article 142 did not apply on these facts. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: possession_ejectment_suit and possession_began_as_servitor_or_servant and possession_was_permissive and hostile_title_not_established_for_limitation_period

predicates.possession_ejectment_suit: A party brought a suit seeking possession by ejecting persons in occupation.
predicates.possession_began_as_servitor_or_servant: The occupants entered or remained in possession in the capacity of servants or servitors.
predicates.possession_was_permissive: The occupants’ possession was initially allowed by the person or institution for whom they served.
predicates.hostile_title_not_established_for_limita: The evidence did not establish possession asserted adversely to the person entitled to the property for the applicable limitation period.
predicates.suit_not_barred_by_adverse_possession: The suit is not barred on the ground that the occupants acquired title by adverse possession.

issues.definition: A possession suit is not barred by adverse possession where the occupants held permissively as servants or servitors and hostile possession for the applicable limitation period was not established.

issues.legal_issue: Servants or servitors who deny the title under which they hold property may be ejected from it.
material_facts: The claimant’s entitlement to manage the property followed from the final tribunal determination.
The defendants were found to be servants or servitors managing or occupying the property on behalf of those entitled to it.
The defendants later asserted a title adverse to the claimant and treated the property as their own.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was entitled to eject the defendants because servitors could not remain in possession after setting up a title adverse to the person on whose behalf they served.
issues.legal_principle: A servant or servitor who repudiates the title under which the property is held forfeits the right to retain possession in that capacity and may be ejected by the person entitled to the property. The Court applied the final tribunal determination and the findings that the defendants were servitors who had asserted an adverse title; it relied on no earlier cases for this proposition.

predicates.possession_ejectment_suit: A party brought a suit seeking possession by ejecting persons in occupation.
predicates.claimant_is_entitled_to_property_managem: The claimant is entitled to manage the property on behalf of those entitled to it.
predicates.occupants_are_servitors: The occupants hold or manage the property as servants or servitors for the person entitled to it.
predicates.occupants_asserted_title_adverse_to_clai: The occupants denied the claimant’s entitlement and asserted a title inconsistent with it.
predicates.servitors_may_be_ejected: Servitors who assert a title adverse to the person for whom they serve may be ejected.

issues.definition: When a claimant is entitled to manage property and its servitors assert a conflicting title, the servitors may be ejected.

issues.legal_issue: A party cannot obtain appellate consideration of a procedural bar based on an earlier dismissed proceeding when the record needed to determine the bar was not developed and no issue was secured for trial.
material_facts: The defendants argued that an earlier possession proceeding dismissed for default barred the later suit.
No trial issue was framed on whether the earlier proceeding and the later suit had the same cause of action.
The parties did not lead evidence on that question or provide a copy of the earlier plaint.
The defendants had failed to obtain a trial issue on the point.
issues.conclusion: The defendants could not raise the asserted bar under Order IX, Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the Court.
issues.legal_principle: Order IX, Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure concerns the bar arising from dismissal of a prior suit for default. The Court declined to consider that bar because no issue had been framed and the record lacked evidence and the earlier plaint needed to determine whether the cause of action was the same.

predicates.possession_suit_with_prior_default_dismi: A party in a possession suit argues that an earlier suit dismissed for default bars the current suit.
predicates.no_trial_issue_on_identity_of_cause: The trial court did not frame an issue asking whether the earlier and current suits involved the same cause of action.
predicates.no_evidence_or_prior_pleading_to_establi: The parties did not provide evidence or the earlier pleading needed to determine whether the causes of action were the same.
predicates.appellant_failed_to_secure_trial_issue: The party raising the bar did not obtain a trial issue on that point.
predicates.prior_dismissal_bar_cannot_be_considered: The appellate court cannot consider the asserted bar on an undeveloped record where the party failed to secure a trial issue.

issues.definition: An appellate court cannot consider a bar based on an earlier dismissal when the party asserting it failed to obtain a trial issue and the record does not establish whether the suits share a cause of action.
